courses.title: Biology Foundations
courses.subject: Biology
courses.description: Explore cells, their parts, and how living things use energy.

modules.title: Module 1 · Cell Structure
objectives: Identify cell membranes, cytoplasm, and nucleus

lesson.title: Inside a Living Cell
lesson.content: A cell is the basic structural and functional unit of living organisms. The cell membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell. Cytoplasm contains structures called organelles, and the nucleus stores most of the cell's genetic information. Plant cells often contain a cell wall and chloroplasts. Animal cells do not have chloroplasts. These structures work together to help cells grow and respond to their environment.

flashcards.back: A selectively permeable boundary that controls what moves in and out of a cell.
An organelle that contains most of a eukaryotic cell's DNA.
An organelle where photosynthesis takes place in plants and algae.

practice.prompt: Which structure controls what enters and leaves a cell?
practice.explanation: The plasma membrane is selectively permeable.

questions.prompt: What is the basic unit of life?
questions.explanation: Cells are the smallest units capable of performing life's basic functions.

questions.prompt: Which structure contains most eukaryotic DNA?
questions.explanation: Most eukaryotic DNA is found in the nucleus.

questions.prompt: Which structure is usually found in plant cells but not animal cells?

lesson.title: How Cells Use Energy
lesson.content: Organisms need energy to carry out life processes. During photosynthesis, plants and algae use light energy to help form glucose from carbon dioxide and water. During cellular respiration, cells break down fuel molecules to make ATP, the molecule that transfers usable energy for many cellular activities. Mitochondria play an important role in aerobic cellular respiration. Photosynthesis and respiration are connected but are not the same process.

flashcards.back: A molecule that transfers usable energy for cellular work.
A process that uses light energy to form energy-rich organic molecules.

practice.prompt: Which molecule transfers usable energy for many cell activities?
practice.explanation: ATP is often called the cell's energy currency.

questions.prompt: In which organelle does much aerobic cellular respiration occur?
Which process uses light energy to produce sugar?

assignments.title: Compare Plant and Animal Cells
assignments.prompt: Write 4–6 sentences comparing the structures of plant and animal cells. Explain one structure they share and one difference.

announcements.title: Welcome to Biology
announcements.body: Start with Module 1. Complete the reading and flashcards before taking the checkpoint exam.

courses.title: English Reading and Writing
courses.subject: English
courses.description: Practice finding main ideas, supporting details, and clear explanations.

modules.title: Module 1 · Main Ideas
objectives: Identify the main idea in a paragraph

lesson.title: Understanding Main Ideas
lesson.content: A main idea is what a paragraph or passage is mostly about. Supporting details explain or prove that main idea. To find the main idea, read the whole paragraph and ask what the author wants the reader to understand. A topic is usually just a few words, but the main idea states a complete thought about the topic. Look for repeated concepts, examples, and a concluding sentence when identifying the author's main point.

flashcards.back: The central point that a passage communicates.
A fact, example, or explanation that supports the main idea.

practice.prompt: What does a supporting detail do?
practice.explanation: A supporting detail gives evidence or explanation for the main idea.

questions.prompt: Which choice best describes a main idea?
Which is most likely a supporting detail?

assignments.title: Summarize a Paragraph
assignments.prompt: Write a short paragraph explaining why it is important to identify a passage's main idea. Include a supporting example.

announcements.title: Reading Practice
announcements.body: Use the flashcards after reading, and practice describing the main idea in your own words.
